messages.author: 48f24841e806e6c6
messages.subject: Custom error messages now supported
parts:
Well a lot of you have been wanting this feature for awhile, and I've never know how to implement it... until today.

Turns out that a Rook user was having trouble getting the app to redirect properly. I actually tracked down the issue to a bug in Rook, but I also realized that rApache needed to do something very basic too: set the status code in the apache request record!

Point is, with the latest commit to rApache, you can now create custom error messages like this:

handler <- function() {
   setContentType("text/plain")
   setStatus(400L)
   cat("Hi, I'm Ale!\n")
   OK
}
 
Notice that setStatus() is a new, undocumented, function that allows you to set the HTTP status. And be sure to return OK rather than returning the status, because if you do then you'll trip the ErrorDocument code in apache which will print out its own custom message.

Hope this helps!

I'll be rolling a new release tomorrow.

Jeff

messages.author: 3ea57457192f4f3b
messages.subject: Re: Custom error messages now supported
parts:
This is a great feature that has been on the wishlist for at least a couple of years :-) First glance, it seems to work. Hopefully no weird side effects. I created a simple test:

jeroen@jeroen-ubuntu:~$ cat /var/www/R/test
cat("this is a test\n")
setStatus(400L)
setHeader(header='X-Powered-By',value='rApache')
return(OK)

And then:

jeroen@jeroen-ubuntu:~R$ curl -v http://localhost/R/test
* About to connect() to localhost port 80 (#0)
*   Trying 127.0.0.1... connected
> GET /R/test HTTP/1.1
> User-Agent: curl/7.22.0 (i686-pc-linux-gnu) libcurl/7.22.0 OpenSSL/1.0.1 zlib/1.2.3.4 libidn/1.23 librtmp/2.3
> Host: localhost
> Accept: */*
>
< HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
< Date: Thu, 10 Jan 2013 23:23:34 GMT
< Server: Apache/2.2.22 (Ubuntu)
< X-Powered-By: rApache
< Connection: close
< Transfer-Encoding: chunked
<
this is a test
* Closing connection #0

messages.subject: Re: Custom error messages now supported
parts:
It is now also possible to do a proper HTTP redirect. Opening the example below in the causes the redirect:

jeroen@jeroen-ubuntu:~$ cat /var/www/R/move 
setStatus(301L)
setHeader("Location", "http://rapache.net")
cat("You are being redirected!!\n\n")
OK


jeroen@jeroen-ubuntu:~$ curl -v http://localhost/R/move

* About to connect() to localhost port 80 (#0)
*   Trying 127.0.0.1... connected
> GET /R/move HTTP/1.1

> User-Agent: curl/7.22.0 (i686-pc-linux-gnu) libcurl/7.22.0 OpenSSL/1.0.1 zlib/1.2.3.4 libidn/1.23 librtmp/2.3
> Host: localhost
> Accept: */*
>

< HTTP/1.1 301 Moved Permanently
< Date: Thu, 10 Jan 2013 23:40:29 GMT
< Server: Apache/2.2.22 (Ubuntu)
< Location: http://rapache.net
< Transfer-Encoding: chunked
< 
You are being redirected!!

messages.author: 48f24841e806e6c6
messages.subject: Re: Custom error messages now supported
parts:
Well, I've chosen not to release today like I said I would. As I started to update the manual for the setStatus() function, I realized that I had yet to deprecate what I said I would deprecate back in 1.1.15:

Changes in 1.1.15

  1. ROutputErrors and RApacheOutputErrors() are deprecated and will be removed in the next release.
  2. The undocumented RPreserveEnv is deprecated.
I doubt anyone is using them, but I'll wait until next week to role a new release to give anyone time to update config files.

Jeff
